title: intent doctor has no acknowledgement mechanism, so a deliberately-kept state warns forever and trains operators to ignore the instrument
body:
## Summary

`intent doctor` has no way to record that a warned-about state is deliberate, so a project that has decided to keep something warns about it on every run, forever.

**Reported by baize-vc** (their `credo_checks` case) during the five-estate Claude Code config sweep, 2026-08-24, and relayed via lamplight-vc. **Lamplight fires the identical warning today**, so it is at least two estates rather than one project's quirk.

## Why this is the same class as a false positive

A permanent alarm about a decision already taken carries no information, and an instrument that is always red trains its operator to stop reading it. This sweep measured the same shape in `/in-autopsy`: it printed a raw banned-word total of 283 where the actionable figure was closer to 14, and every estate had learned to discount the number rather than act on it.

**The cost is not the noise. It is that a real finding arriving on that channel is indistinguishable from the standing one.**

## Close condition

`intent doctor` can be told a specific check is acknowledged for this project, the acknowledgement is recorded where a reader can see it and audit it, and an acknowledged check stops warning without being silently dropped from the roster -- a check that disappears is worse than one that shouts.

Deliberately NOT proposed here: whether the acknowledgement lives in config, in canon, or beside the check. That is a design call for hv.
